page.layout: One page of text, one column, with a running head at the top. A full-width heading "De unione naturarum." opens the page, followed by short paragraphs, a second heading "Ex Maria." and more short paragraphs. No marginal notes. The last line is followed by a catchword at the right.

main_text.head: De unione naturarum.

p.i: Naturam humanam in Christo a divina fuis-se absorptam, Eutychiani, Iacobitæ, Armenij.

main_text.p: Naturam humanam deificatam, i. mutatam in divinam & illi adæquatam fuisse, Nestoriani, Servetani, Ubiquitarij.
Ex duabus naturis unum quiddam mixtū & tertium factum esse in Christo, Timotheani.
Quod tertium, alij dicunt mortale fuisse, ne-pe Theodotiani: alij immortale, nempe, Caiani.
Filium Dei in filiū Mariæ descendisse in Baptismo, ɔ[?]Manichæi.
Verbum ipsum Dei in carnem esse mutatum, ɔ[?]Apollinaristæ.
Divinam naturam in Christo passam esse, Theopaschitæ.
Divinam naturam & humanam manere quidē in Christo, sed earum proprietates esse confusas, ɔ[?]Acephali, Severitæ.
Christum, quatenus homo, non habere propriam voluntatem, quia confusa fit humana natura & versa in divinam, ɔ[?]Apollinaristæ.
Unam tantūm in Christo voluntatem fuisse, Monothelitæ.
main_text.head: Ex Maria.
main_text.p: Christum negant ex Maria assumpsisse corpus, Valentiniani, Secundiani, ɔ[?]Apollinaristæ.
Christum ex Davidis semine esse negant Tatiani, ɔ[?]Manichæi.
Christum ex Maria virgine natum negant hominem verum fuisse, & passum, quia caro hu-mana

page.notes: The sign before some names (rendered ɔ[?]) is a stylised mark that could not be read with certainty. Words reading "ff" are long s and have been transcribed as s. The catchword "mana" is partly cut off at the edge; the reading is uncertain. No page number is printed.
